newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Markets prove doomsters wrong on Swedish EMU "no".
newsitem.headline: Markets prove doomsters wrong on Swedish EMU "no".

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Monday that developments on financial markets since Stockholm decided not to join the single European currency from the start had proven the "prophets of doom" wrong.

Asbrink noted that Swedish bond yields had plunged and the crown had strengthened against the dollar and the mark since the ruling Social Democrats decided last month against early entry of economic and monetary union (EMU).

"The development has been very positive for Sweden since the decision was announced and that would hardly have been the case if it had been seen as very negative," Asbrink told reporters after a meeting of European Union finance ministers in Brussels.
"I can't see that we need to regret anything about our actions or about our position."

The Social Democrat's party board said on June 3 that its decision to stay out from the start, expected to be confirmed by parliament later this year, was largely due to public opposition to EMU. But it left the door open to join at a later date.
Asbrink noted that Swedish 10-year bond yields had declined by more than 50 basis points to below 6.50 percent since the move was announced.
This reflected growing confidence in the Swedish economy, he said, adding that he believed there was room for a further narrowing of the gap in Swedish bond yields compared with those abroad.
That gap has already fallen to around 90 basis points compared with German bond yields, the smallest difference ever.
Asbrink also said that when there was uncertainty surrounding the EMU project, as there has been recently, it was not a disadvantage to have taken the position Sweden did.

"There is reason to note that we hold our own very well in the present situation, in the development which has taken place," he said. This had been demonstrated in the lower bond yields and a stronger crown.
Asbrink said the EMU project was still uncertain in some respects. Because of this, several observers believed Sweden had made a fairly wise decision, he added.
But he stressed that he did not hope for a troublesome development for EMU, adding it was important that it came into being and that it was successful.

Sweden had no reason to hope for a weak euro, he said. "It is important that there is a relatively strict interpretation of the criteria and that it therefore becomes a strong and stable currency," he said.
